agent_vs_you: The plan shape matches the catalogue rule I would follow too: one lettered image per size from the same brief, not crops. Square and portrait came out right. The landscape's first qwen render had all five strings but two were garbled ('20% off n / all indoor plants', 'Saturday, 8. Sunday') because all five lines were squeezed into a half-width column of a 640x360 canvas. The harness's one fix then made it strictly worse. Its prompt asked qwen to 'read exactly "20% off all indoor plants"' while also 'remove the Discount block, first line … entirely' and 'remove … second line … entirely'. qwen deleted the discount and wrote 'Saturday & Sunday' where it had been, the garbled date stayed, and nobody re-read the result before the node was marked done. My prompts would differ in two ways. They would state the user's 'green-and-cream' (the agent's three prompts never mention a colour, and the palette came out right only by luck) and give each shape an explicit layout: in 16:9, the text panel takes two-thirds of the width with one short line per string, so the type stays large. The decisive defect is the fix step, the same one that sank A03d.

your_plan.say: I'll make three matching green-and-cream plant-shop ads, square, tall and wide, each laid out for its shape so all five lines, including the address, stay large and easy to read.

steps.why: Two-thirds of the 640x360 width for text keeps the type size up. The garbling came from a half-width column.

fix: Same harness fix as A03d, in execute.js and buildable.js fixText. A garbled rendering of a WANTED string is a misspelling to correct in place, never a 'stray' to remove; fixText must not send 'remove … entirely' for something it is also asked to write. Fix one string per edit, naming its position. Re-read after the fix, with up to 2 rounds, and choose between the before and after images by the readback: here the 'before' had 5 of 5 strings present, the 'after' 4. Flag the node instead of reporting 'lettering fixed' when it still misreads. Also add a palette guard so the user's stated colours enter every image prompt (see G34b).
